DrinfeldModulesAndTModules.summary: The baseline contains essentially none of this roadmap's mathematics. Its one real asset is Mathlib's new `SkewPolynomial` ring (Mathlib/Algebra/SkewPolynomial/Basic.lean, explicitly modelled on Papikian's Drinfeld-modules book): for a ring with a `MulSemiringAction (Multiplicative ℕ)` — e.g. L with the q-power Frobenius, an action that still has to be supplied — it is the Ore ring L{τ} with τa = a^qτ, with the ring structure and the commutation rule proved. Nothing else is there: no Drinfeld module, no Carlitz module, no torsion or Tate module, no exponential/lattice uniformization, no moduli stack, no t-module or t-motive, no Tate/Taguchi theorem, no Taelman class-number formula, no elliptic sheaves, no Frobenius-difference Tannakian category. Peripheral tools exist and are the honest starting points — Mathlib's ℂ_p and characteristic-free spectral norm (C_∞ is blocked by the missing normed structure on F_q((1/t)) and the characteristic-zero hypothesis of `IsAlgClosed.of_denseRange`), Tate algebras, the transcendence-degree API, Dedekind-domain and DVR theory, and Tau Ceti's affine group schemes over any base (G_a with its Frobenius endomorphism, kernels of isogenies as finite flat group schemes, Cartier duality, Tannakian reconstruction for commutative Hopf algebras) — but they supply no theorem this roadmap states.

targets.target: The Ore ring L{tau} with tau a = a^q tau
targets.note: Mathlib's `SkewPolynomial R` is `SkewMonoidAlgebra R (Multiplicative ℕ)`; the twist φ is carried by a `MulSemiringAction (Multiplicative ℕ) R`, and `X_mul`/`monomial_mul_monomial` give Xa = φ(a)X. Instantiating φ as the q-power Frobenius of L gives L{τ}; the file's docstring cites Papikian's Drinfeld-modules book, chapter 3, and the δ = 0 case of Ore. No such Frobenius action instance is provided (it has to be supplied, e.g. through the action of L →+* L on L), `SkewPolynomial` is used nowhere else in either library, and no degree function, left/right division algorithm or Euclidean theory is developed, so only the ring itself is there.

targets.target: Identification of L{tau} with the F_q-linear polynomial endomorphisms of G_a (additive polynomials)
targets.note: `grep -rn -i 'additive polynomial'` returns nothing in either tree, and there is no ring map from `SkewPolynomial` to `Polynomial` or to endomorphisms of G_a sending τ to the q-power map. Tau Ceti has the additive group scheme over any commutative base with its p-power Frobenius endomorphism on points (`AdditiveGroup.frobeniusEnd`) and α_p as the kernel of Frobenius (`AlphaP.range_inclusion`), but End(G_a) is not made a ring and there is no theory of additive/F_q-linear polynomials.

targets.target: Rank-r Drinfeld A-module: characteristic map A → L, deg φ_a = r·deg a, nonzero constant term
targets.note: No occurrence of `Drinfeld` in either library outside `CategoryTheory/Monoidal/Center.lean` (the Drinfeld centre of a monoidal category, an unrelated notion). The degree normalization at infinity is likewise absent.

targets.target: Morphisms, isogenies and kernels of Drinfeld modules as group schemes
targets.note: Tau Ceti has affine group schemes over a commutative base ring via commutative Hopf algebras, with kernels as closed subgroup schemes (`kernelSpec`), finite faithfully flat kernels of isogenies, fppf quotients and Cartier duality, but nothing attached to a Drinfeld module; the kernel group scheme of φ_a is not constructed anywhere.

targets.target: Drinfeld modules over a general base via line bundles with invertible leading coefficients (moduli functor)
targets.note: Absent; there is no relative version of any of the above, and no line-bundle-valued additive group scheme.

targets.target: The Carlitz module t ↦ theta + tau, its rank, multiplication and kernel degree
targets.note: `grep -rn -i carlitz` returns nothing in either tree.

duplicates.note: FF.4 mentions additive polynomials over finite fields among 'finite rings, sequences and codes'; the F_q-linear polynomial ring is the shared object, although FF.4 wants it for coding theory rather than for a Drinfeld module.

targets.target: Ideal torsion φ[a] of a Drinfeld module and its finite flatness of the expected degree
targets.note: Flatness and finite locally free modules are in Mathlib in full generality, but there is no Drinfeld module to take torsion of, so the statement does not exist.

targets.target: Etaleness of a-torsion away from the characteristic ideal; inseparability at the characteristic
targets.note: Mathlib has formally étale/unramified/smooth algebras and étale morphisms of schemes; none of this is applied to torsion of a Drinfeld module.

targets.target: Tate module T_lambda(phi) as an inverse limit of lambda-power torsion, free of rank r over A_lambda
targets.note: `grep -rn -i 'tate module'` returns nothing in either library — there is no Tate module even for elliptic curves, let alone for Drinfeld modules.

targets.target: Continuous Galois action on the Tate module
targets.note: Tau Ceti has continuous cohomology of smooth discrete Galois modules (`TauCeti/RepresentationTheory/Homological/ContCohomology/`), but no Tate module carrying such an action.

targets.target: Separate treatment of the local object at the characteristic prime (connected part not visible in separable points)
targets.note: Absent. Tau Ceti has the identity component of an affine algebraic group and represents the fppf quotient G/G° by the finite étale constant group π₀(G) (`componentGroupFppfGroupObjectIso`), but only over an algebraically closed field; there is no connected–étale sequence over a general field or base, which is what separating the connected part from the separable points requires.

targets.target: The completed algebraic closure C_infinity of K_infinity with its generic-characteristic embedding
targets.note: Mathlib builds ℂ_p exactly this way — the completion of an algebraic closure of ℚ_p with the spectral norm (`PadicComplex`) — and the spectral norm on an algebraic extension of a complete nonarchimedean normed field (`spectralNorm.normedField`) has no characteristic hypothesis. Two pieces are missing for C_∞: `RatFunc.CompletionAtInfty` (K_∞ = F_q((1/t))) carries only a `Valued ℤᵐ⁰` structure, with no normed-field or rank-one instance, and `IsAlgClosed.of_denseRange`, which makes the completion algebraically closed, assumes characteristic zero. The generic-characteristic embedding of A is not stated.

targets.target: The Drinfeld exponential: entire, solving the functional equation, surjective
targets.note: Absent. There is no nonarchimedean entire-function theory (no Weierstrass products, no Newton polygons: `grep -i 'newton polygon'` is empty) on which such a construction could rest.

targets.target: Kernel of the exponential is a discrete projective A-lattice of rank r
targets.note: Mathlib's lattice notions are `IsZLattice` (a discrete ℤ-submodule spanning a normed space) and the purely algebraic `Submodule.IsLattice` (finitely generated and spanning, with no discreteness); there is no discrete A-lattice in K_∞ or C_∞, and no projectivity statement in this setting.

targets.target: The inverse lattice-to-module functor and independence under homothety
targets.note: Absent.

targets.target: Carlitz exponential recurrence and period lattice
targets.note: Absent.

targets.target: The moduli stack of rank-r Drinfeld modules and fine level-structure schemes away from the characteristic
targets.note: Absent. Neither library has algebraic stacks at all: Mathlib's only `Stack` notion is `CategoryTheory.Pseudofunctor.IsStackFor` (descent for pseudofunctors on a site, Mathlib/CategoryTheory/Sites/Descent/DescentData.lean:507), which is the abstract stack condition, not a moduli stack.

targets.target: Representability and smoothness of the level moduli over the stated open base
targets.note: Absent.

targets.target: Hecke correspondences on Drinfeld modular varieties
targets.note: Absent. Abstract Hecke rings of a Hecke pair exist for any group (Mathlib `HeckeRing`, and Tau Ceti's double-coset rings with GL_n instances), but there are no Drinfeld modular varieties to define correspondences on.

targets.target: Pink's generic-fibre Satake compactification via generalized Drinfeld modules, and its uniqueness
targets.note: Absent.

targets.target: The ample line bundle of Drinfeld modular forms and change-of-level pullback/pushforward
targets.note: Absent.

targets.target: Anderson t-module on G_a^d with differential theta·Id + nilpotent
targets.note: Absent; `grep -rn -i anderson` in the Lean sources matches only unrelated names (Anderson-type results in topology/probability), never a t-module.

targets.target: The motive of a t-module: F_q-linear maps to G_a, contravariant convention, tau action, finite generation
targets.note: Absent. The underlying skew-polynomial module structure could be expressed with `SkewPolynomial` but no such module is defined.

targets.target: Equivalence of abelian t-modules with effective Anderson motives (inverse functors and Hom maps)
targets.note: Absent.

targets.target: Purity, rigid analytic triviality and uniformizability as separate properties
targets.note: Absent: no notion of purity, rigid analytic triviality or uniformizability exists. The analytic base is only partly there: Tate algebras (Mathlib `MvPowerSeries.IsRestricted.subring`; Tau Ceti `Huber.restrictedMvPowerSeriesSubring`, strictly topologically finite type algebras and the adic closed polydisc), but no rigid analytic spaces.

targets.target: The Carlitz motive and its tensor powers
targets.note: Absent.

targets.target: The natural map Hom_L(phi,psi) ⊗_A A_lambda → Hom_Galois(T_lambda phi, T_lambda psi)
targets.note: Absent: neither the Hom module of Drinfeld modules nor the Tate module exists.

targets.target: Injectivity of that map
targets.note: Absent.

targets.target: Surjectivity (the Tate conjecture for Drinfeld modules / t-motives, Taguchi–Tamagawa)
targets.note: Absent. No analogue of Tate's isogeny theorem exists in either library even for abelian varieties.

targets.target: Semisimplicity of the rational Tate representation
targets.note: Absent.

targets.target: Taelman's convergent Euler-product L-value for an integral Drinfeld module
targets.note: Mathlib's Euler products are indexed by the primes of ℕ, for multiplicative functions valued in a complete normed field or ring; Tau Ceti adds formal Euler products over the primes of a number field. There is no characteristic-p Goss L-value, no product over the monic irreducibles of A or the closed points of a curve, and no convergence statement in C_∞.

targets.target: The exponential unit lattice U(phi/A) and the finite class module H(phi/A)
targets.note: Absent.

targets.target: Normalized lattice covolume and Fitting polynomial of the class module
targets.note: Absent; Mathlib has no Fitting ideals of modules at all (the only `Fitting` names are Lie-theoretic `posFittingComp`).

targets.target: The determinant / nuclear-operator identity
targets.note: Absent.

targets.target: Taelman's class-number formula
targets.note: Absent. Tau Ceti does prove finiteness of the divisor class group and defines a function-field class number (`TauCeti.Divisor.classNumber`, TauCeti/FieldTheory/FunctionField/RiemannRoch/ClassNumber.lean:202), but that is the classical Pic^0, not Taelman's class module, and there is no special-value identity.

targets.target: The chain of vector bundles with Frobenius modification attached to a Drinfeld module (elliptic sheaf)
targets.note: Absent; `grep -rn -i shtuka` and `grep -rn -i 'elliptic sheaf'` return nothing in either tree.

targets.target: Distinguished pole at infinity, characteristic leg and periodicity conditions
targets.note: Absent.

targets.target: The elliptic-sheaf equivalence with Drinfeld modules in its normalized range
targets.note: Absent.

targets.target: Prime-to-characteristic Tate realizations, and local-shtuka comparison interfaces
targets.note: Absent.

duplicates.note: DM.7 explicitly exports its construction as the rank-r special case of GS.2's global shtuka stacks; both state the Frobenius-modification definition, and neither is in the libraries.
The local-shtuka and comparison interfaces DM.7 promises are the objects HS2 constructs (local shtuka moduli and bounds); the overlap is the local realization, not the global elliptic sheaf.

targets.target: Neutral Tannakian category of rigid analytically trivial pre-t-motives with its fibre functor
targets.note: Tau Ceti proves Tannakian reconstruction in the Hopf-algebra direction — the points functor of a commutative Hopf algebra is isomorphic to the tensor-automorphism functor of its comodule category — but there is no general 'neutral Tannakian category ⇒ affine group scheme' theorem, and no category of t-motives to apply it to.

targets.target: The Frobenius-difference Galois group of a t-motive
targets.note: Absent; there is no difference- or differential-Galois (Picard–Vessiot) theory in either library.

targets.target: The analytic trivialization matrix and the specialization/lifting criterion identifying period transcendence degree with the group dimension
targets.note: Absent.

targets.target: Algebraic independence of Carlitz logarithms of algebraic arguments under linear independence
targets.note: Mathlib has the algebraic-independence and transcendence-degree API (transcendence bases, `Algebra.trdeg` and its additivity in towers) and Liouville's theorem, but no transcendence theorem for periods or logarithms in any characteristic, and there is no Carlitz logarithm.

duplicates.note: States the same Tannakian package — tensor automorphism groups of a fibre functor, torsors between two fibre functors, pro-algebraic reconstruction and period torsors — for motives rather than for rigid analytically trivial t-motives.

FunctionFieldArithmetic.summary: This is by far the best-covered roadmap in the batch, because Tau Ceti has already built Stichtenoth's theory of algebraic function fields: `TauCeti.Place` (normalized discrete valuations trivial on the constants, with residue fields, degrees, weak and strong approximation, finiteness of places of bounded degree, and the bijection with the height-one primes of a Dedekind affine model), divisors with the product formula `deg (div f) = 0`, Riemann--Roch spaces, the genus, Weil differentials and the full Riemann--Roch theorem with the canonical class of degree 2g-2, finiteness of Cl^0 over a finite constant field, and an e/f/decomposition/inertia/lower-ramification-group/different theory of finite extensions, all sorry-free. So FA.1 is largely done, FA.0 is done on the function-field side but not on the curve side (there is no curve object, so no scheme-theoretic closed points, normalization of P^1 in F or finite morphisms of curves), and FA.3 is half done. What is genuinely missing is everything analytic and adelic: the adele ring of a function field with its topology (Mathlib has `RestrictedProduct` and the finite adeles of a Dedekind domain, and Tau Ceti makes each finite completion a local field), discreteness and cocompactness, self-dual measures and Poisson summation, the idele degree map and compactness of the degree-zero idele class group; so FA.2 has a partial for every construction but no target in full and is not built. Then all of class field theory for function fields (Tau Ceti has class-formation scaffolding, Tate cohomology, and for number fields ray class groups and the ideal-theoretic Artin map, but no reciprocity law), the zeta function of a curve and Artin L-factors, function-field Chebotarev, and the entire automorphic layer FA.6. Riemann--Hurwitz, upper-numbering ramification, the wild half of Dedekind's different theorem, and Artin--Schreier/Witt descriptions of p-power cyclic extensions are also absent, and FA.7's certified algorithms are not there.

targets.target: One-variable function fields over a base field, as an intrinsic predicate
targets.note: Tau Ceti's intrinsic `IsFunctionField k F` (transcendence degree one plus essential finite type) is proved equivalent to Mathlib's chosen-generator `FunctionField F K`, and is stable under finite extension. No hypothesis that k is finite or perfect.

targets.target: Closed points identified with discrete valuations trivial on the constants
targets.note: `Place k F` is a surjective `Valuation F ℤᵐ⁰` trivial on kˣ; its valuation ring is a DVR and determines the place. The ideal-theoretic dictionary is built: places finite on a Dedekind affine model R correspond to `HeightOneSpectrum R` (`Place.heightOneSpectrumEquiv`), and the places of k(x) are the monic irreducibles plus ∞ (`Place.ratFuncEquiv`). Missing: the projective curve itself, hence the identification of places with its scheme-theoretic closed points.

targets.target: Normalization of a projective model; the contravariant equivalence between one-variable function fields and smooth projective curves over a perfect field
targets.note: The affine half is there: the integral closure of k[x] in F is a Dedekind domain with fraction field F, and its height-one primes correspond to the places not at infinity. Mathlib defines the function field of an integral scheme as the stalk at the generic point. Missing entirely: gluing the two affine normalizations into a projective curve, properness, and the anti-equivalence of categories — there is no `Curve` object in either tree over which to state it.

targets.target: The exact constant field, and its finiteness when k is finite
targets.note: The constant field k̃ = algebraicClosure k F is finite-dimensional over k, and F/k̃ is a function field with exact constants. Over a finite k, Mathlib's `Module.finite_of_finite` turns finite-dimensionality into finiteness of k̃, so the finite-field case is covered by the general statements (it is not stated separately). `algebraicClosure_ratFunc` is the F_q(t) acceptance case.

targets.target: Geometric connectedness after choosing the exact constant field
targets.note: Mathlib has `GeometricallyConnected` for scheme morphisms and Tau Ceti has the constant compositum and geometric degree of a function-field extension, but the theorem 'exact constants ⇒ the curve is geometrically connected' (equivalently F ⊗_k k̄ is a field) is not proved anywhere.

targets.target: Finite morphisms from finite field extensions, with inseparable degree and induced residue-field maps
targets.note: The place-level shadow is built: every place of the base extends (`restrict_surjective`), with e and f, the tower formulas, the residue-field extension, and the inseparable residue degree in the inertia count. Missing: the curves, hence the finite morphism C' → C attached to F'/F and its degree decomposition.

duplicates.note: Identical targets: the `IsFunctionField` predicate, the constant field k̃ and its finiteness over k, and places as normalized valuations trivial on constants — this Tau Ceti layer is what produced the declarations cited above.
Owns the normalization of k[x] in F including the inseparable case, and the places-to-height-one-primes dictionary that FA.0's 'normalization of a projective model' rests on.
Owns exactly FA.0's remaining target, the contravariant dictionary between function fields and (regular, not smooth) projective curves, including the normalization of P^1 in F.
Owns the places of k(x) and the fact that k is the exact constant field of k(x) — FA.0's 'recover P^1 from F_q(t)' acceptance case.

Owns constant-field extensions with exact constants preserved (Stichtenoth 3.6.1) and the absolute-irreducibility criterion for exact constants (3.6.6–3.6.8) — FA.0's geometric-connectedness target in function-field form.

targets.target: Divisors, effectivity, and degree weighted by residue degrees
targets.note: `Divisor k F` is the free abelian group on places with `degree` weighted by `Place.degree`, with effectivity, lattice operations, positive/negative parts, the conorm along a finite extension and the cross-multiplied degree identity.

targets.target: The principal divisor map and the product formula deg(div f) = 0
targets.note: `deg (f)_∞ = [F : k(f)]` (`Divisor.degree_poles`, and `degree_zeros` for the zero divisor) gives `degree_principal : deg (div f) = 0`, hence the degree map on the class group; `div f = 0` iff f is algebraic over k.

targets.target: Riemann--Roch spaces L(D) and their dimensions
targets.note: L(D) is finite-dimensional with the bound ℓ(D) ≤ deg D₊ + 1, monotone, and invariant under linear equivalence; `Divisor.dim` is ℓ.

targets.target: Canonical divisors, the canonical class and deg K = 2g-2
targets.note: Built from Weil differentials (linear forms on the repartition space vanishing on A(D)+F); ℓ(W)=g and deg W = 2g-2 are proved, under the standing hypotheses `IsFunctionField k F` and `IsIntegrallyClosedIn k F` (exact constants).

targets.target: The Riemann--Roch theorem
targets.note: `ℓ(D) = deg D + 1 - g + ℓ(W-D)` for every D, with W the divisor of any nonzero Weil differential (Stichtenoth 1.5.15), plus the deg D ≥ 2g-1 corollary. Proved without sorry; hypotheses are `IsFunctionField k F` and exact constants, with no finiteness assumption on k — more general than FA.1's F_q setting.

targets.target: Finiteness of Pic^0 over a finite constant field
targets.note: `finite_ker_degreeClass` is exactly 'Cl⁰(F) is finite for a finite constant field' (Stichtenoth 5.1.3), with the class number defined and positive; the affine class group of a holomorphy ring is also finite.

targets.target: Rational divisor classes versus chosen rational points
targets.note: The distinction is respected throughout: hypotheses are stated as 'a divisor of degree one' and the existence of a degree-one *place* is derived only where Riemann--Roch produces it (genus 0 and genus 1 cases).

targets.target: Residue maps
targets.note: What exists is the *local component* ω_P of a Weil differential and the abstract residue theorem ∑_P ω_P(x) = 0 (the file's own docstring says this holds 'before any residue map has been constructed'). The residue map Res_P : Ω_F → k on Kähler differentials and its comparison with Weil differentials (Stichtenoth IV.3) are not built: `Kaehler.lean` only proves dim_F Ω[F/k] = 1 for a separating element and sets up the derivative.

targets.target: Bases of L(D) from certified presentations (an algorithm)
targets.note: Only the explicit P^1 computation L(n·∞) = polynomials of degree ≤ n exists (an acceptance case of FA.1); there is no algorithm computing a basis of L(D) on a general curve and no certificate format.

duplicates.note: States FA.1's divisors, product formula, L(D), Riemann's theorem and the genus verbatim (Stichtenoth I.4); it is the roadmap that produced Tau Ceti's `Divisor`/`riemannRochSpace`/`genus`.
Owns Riemann--Roch itself via repartitions and Weil differentials — the theorem FA.1 asks to 'transport'.
Owns the deg D ≥ 2g-1 regime, strong approximation and the local components that FA.1 calls residue maps.
Owns exactly FA.1's missing piece: the residue map on Kähler differentials and its comparison with the Weil formalism.
FA.1 says it transports 'the curve Riemann--Roch theorem' from SF.3; both layers state Riemann--Roch, one on schemes and one on function fields.
States the same places/divisors/divisor-class-group dictionary, specialized to the function field of an elliptic curve, and consumes it for the Weil pairing.

targets.target: The adele ring of K as a restricted product of local completions with respect to their valuation rings
targets.note: The general restricted-product construction and the finite adeles of a Dedekind domain (hence of an affine model of the curve, with adic completions and their integer rings) are in Mathlib. What is missing is the adele ring of a function field itself: the places at infinity are not adjoined, and Tau Ceti's `repartitionSpace` is the completion-free repartition space, not a topological ring.

targets.target: Local compactness of the adele ring
targets.note: The general criterion (each factor locally compact, the distinguished subgroups open and almost all compact) is proved for restricted products, and Tau Ceti makes every adic completion with finite residue field a nonarchimedean local field (so locally compact, with compact integers), which covers the finite places of a function field over F_q. Local compactness of a function-field adele ring would follow once the ring is constructed; the instance itself is not in the libraries.

targets.target: Discreteness and cocompactness of K in its additive adeles
targets.note: Discreteness and closedness of the diagonal are proved for number fields only, and cocompactness is not proved even there. For function fields Tau Ceti proves the algebraic shadow — A(D) ∩ F = L(D) and dim_k A_F/(A_F(D)+F) = i(D) < ∞ — which is the finite-dimensionality behind cocompactness, but with no topology on the repartition space.

targets.target: The idele group, the idele degree map and the compact degree-zero idele class group
targets.note: Mathlib defines the idele and idele class groups of a number field but proves nothing about them; there is no degree map, no degree-zero subgroup and no compactness statement, and nothing at all in the function-field case.

targets.target: Local residue characters from a nonzero differential and self-dual Haar measures
targets.note: The ambient machinery is more general than one might expect: Mathlib has Haar measure on any locally compact group, `AddChar` valued in the circle, and `VectorFourier.fourierIntegral` for an arbitrary commutative ring 𝕜 with a unitary additive character, a bilinear pairing and a measure — so the adelic Fourier integral is expressible. What is missing is everything specific: no additive character of a positive-characteristic local field built from a residue, no self-duality of a measure, and Fourier inversion only for finite abelian groups (`ZMod.dft_dft`, `AddChar.doubleDualEquiv`) and finite-dimensional real inner product spaces.

targets.target: The global residue pairing and Poisson summation on the adeles
targets.note: Mathlib's Poisson summation is ∑_{n∈ℤ} f(n) = ∑ 𝓕f(n) on ℝ with decay hypotheses. Pontryagin duality is proved only for finite abelian groups (`AddChar.doubleDualEquiv`, with Fourier inversion `ZMod.dft_dft`) and the circle (Tau Ceti); there is none for general LCA groups, no adelic Fourier transform and no adelic Poisson summation.

duplicates.note: The same construction and the same discreteness/cocompactness statements, for number fields; FA.2 explicitly says the archimedean arguments cannot be imported unchanged, so the overlap is in the statements, not the proofs.
Owns the idele group and the idele class group in the number-field case, including strong approximation.
AA.1 constructs adelic points of algebraic groups over a global field as restricted products with their topology; the underlying adele ring and its local compactness are shared with FA.2.
Owns the repartition (completion-free adele) space and the filtration A_F(D), which FA.2 re-uses as the algebraic skeleton of its adele ring.

Owns restricted products of locally compact groups: local compactness, compact-open cylinders and restricted products of Haar measures normalized on almost all places — exactly FA.2's first two targets in group-theoretic generality.

targets.target: Integral closures in finite separable extensions and the places above a place
targets.note: The fundamental identity ∑ e_i f_i = [F':F] is proved (separably, and on an affine model), together with Kummer's factorization theorem and integral bases.

targets.target: Decomposition and inertia groups
targets.note: Galois transitivity on the fibre, the decomposition field with its degree, and the inertia group with |I| = e·(inseparable residue degree) are all proved for place extensions of function fields.

targets.target: The different and the discriminant
targets.note: Dedekind's different theorem is proved in part: d(P'|P) ≥ e−1 always, and d = e−1 at tame places with separable residue extension, plus transitivity in towers. The converse half (d ≥ e at wild places, Stichtenoth 3.5.1(b)/3.5.5) is only remarked in a docstring. Mathlib supplies `differentIdeal` and the discriminant underneath. The wild different is therefore bounded below but not computed.

targets.target: Lower and upper ramification filtrations
targets.note: Only the lower-numbering filtration G_i is built, with the quotient embeddings into the residue field and the p-group structure of G_1. The Herbrand function φ/ψ and the upper numbering are absent from both libraries, so the wild conductor computation FA.3's acceptance demands is not available.

targets.target: Riemann--Hurwitz including the wild different
targets.note: Absent: `grep -rn -i hurwitz` matches only Hurwitz zeta functions in Mathlib. The different divisor exists, but 2g'-2 = [F':F](2g-2) + deg Diff(F'/F) is not stated anywhere; note also that Tau Ceti's genus theory is in place, so this is a missing theorem rather than missing vocabulary.

targets.target: Artin--Schreier and Witt-vector descriptions of cyclic p-power extensions
targets.note: Mathlib has Witt vectors and Frobenius/Verschiebung but no Artin--Schreier theory (its Kummer-extension file lists it as a TODO): the only `artinSchreier` names are characteristic-2 quadratic-splitting lemmas in Tau Ceti (a general polynomial file and the elliptic-curve node polynomial). The classification of ℤ/p-extensions by F/℘(F) and of ℤ/p^n-extensions by Witt vectors is absent, as is the equivalence relation on the defining elements.

targets.target: Purely inseparable extensions by Frobenius, treated separately
targets.note: Mathlib's general purely inseparable field theory is available, Tau Ceti keeps the inseparable residue degree visible in the inertia count, and over a finite constant field Tau Ceti computes the Frobenius subfield degrees [K(X) : K(X)^q] = q (and the same for an elliptic function field). There is no general treatment of F^{1/p}/F for a function field: no [F : F^p] = p, and nothing on its places, genus, different or the absence of a Galois or étale-cover interpretation.

duplicates.note: Owns e, f, the fundamental identity, the conorm and the decomposition theory that FA.3 restates.
Owns both the different (already built) and the Hurwitz genus formula (FA.3's missing target), from the same Stichtenoth sections FA.3 cites via Rosen.
Owns constant-field extensions and the inseparability traps that FA.3 says must be treated separately.

Owns the lower-numbering filtration G_i of a local field, the Herbrand functions φ/ψ and the upper numbering with its quotient theorem — FA.3's filtration target, locally; its upper-numbering half is not built.

Owns Kummer and Artin–Schreier covers y^p − y = u with their ramification, different and genus formulas (Stichtenoth 3.7.8–3.7.10) — FA.3's Artin–Schreier target and its y^p − y = t^{-m} acceptance case.

targets.target: Local reciprocity for F_{q^d}((t)): the local Artin map and its norm-subgroup description

GlobalShtukasAndFunctionFieldLanglands.summary: Nothing in this roadmap is in the pinned libraries. Neither Mathlib nor Tau Ceti has algebraic stacks (Mathlib's only `Stack` notion is the abstract descent condition `CategoryTheory.Pseudofunctor.IsStackFor`), loop groups, affine or Beilinson--Drinfeld Grassmannians, perverse sheaves, intersection cohomology, shtukas, Drinfeld's lemma, or excursion operators; `grep -rn -i shtuka` and `grep -rn -i satake` are both empty across the two trees. What does exist is foundational and genuinely useful: Mathlib now carries the étale, fppf, fpqc and pro-étale topologies on schemes and a definition of ℓ-adic cohomology as pro-étale cohomology with ℤ_ℓ-coefficients (`AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.EllAdicCohomology`), together with faithfully flat descent for modules and descent of morphism properties along flat quasi-compact surjections; Tau Ceti has reductive affine group schemes, root data and fppf quotients. But no cohomological theorem — finiteness, base change, duality, the trace formula — is proved for ℓ-adic cohomology, so even GS.3's coefficient formalism is unavailable. Every layer is not built.

Tau Ceti's reductive groups are affine group schemes over a field given by Hopf algebras, not smooth group schemes over a curve.

BunGAndNewtonStrata.summary: This roadmap lives on the Fargues--Fontaine curve over perfectoid spaces, and that setting does not exist in the pinned baseline: Mathlib has the tilting/untilting fragment (`PreTilt.untilt`, `WittVector.fontaineTheta`, `BDeRham`) but no perfectoid ring or space, and Tau Ceti has adic spaces `Spa(A,A⁺)` of Huber pairs but no diamonds, no v-stacks, no Fargues--Fontaine curve. The one genuine asset is Mathlib's `WittVector.Isocrystal`: isocrystals over W(k)[1/p] with φ-semilinear automorphisms are defined and the Dieudonné--Manin classification is proved in dimension one (`WittVector.isocrystal_classification`), which is the GL_1 shadow of BG0's B(G). Tau Ceti supplies reductive affine group schemes, root data with isogenies and dominant cones, parabolic and Levi subgroups of cocharacters, Tannakian reconstruction for commutative Hopf algebras, and fppf torsor quotients — real inputs for the group-theoretic half of BG0 and BG1, but no σ-conjugacy classes, no Kottwitz map, no Newton cocharacter, no Bun_G and no strata. Every layer is not built.

targets.note: There is no perfectoid ring or space in Mathlib (only the untilt map and Fontaine's θ) and no Fargues--Fontaine curve in either tree, so there is no base on which to define a G-torsor. Tau Ceti has fppf torsors under an affine group scheme over a field, which is the algebraic prototype only.

targets.note: The pieces of the Tannakian comparison exist in the affine algebraic setting: Tau Ceti proves that the points of a commutative Hopf algebra are the tensor automorphisms of its comodule category, Mathlib has the étale and fpqc topologies and faithfully flat descent for modules. The comparison of the three torsor notions over an analytic base, and the equivalence with exact tensor functors into vector bundles, are not proved.

There is no slope decomposition in higher rank, no G-isocrystal for a general reductive G, no σ-conjugacy set B(G) and no ramified/unequal-characteristic version.

ExcursionOperatorsAndSpectralAction.summary: Almost nothing this roadmap states is in the pinned libraries; the one general construction present is Mathlib's centre of a category (`CategoryTheory.CatCenter`, with its linear scalar map), which ES0 would apply to D_lis(Bun_G). Its whole setting — lisse sheaves on Artin v-stacks, coherent Hecke kernels, the stack of Langlands parameters, the Bernstein centre, smooth representations of a p-adic group, local Langlands — is absent: `grep -rn -i` finds no `satake`, no `bernstein center`, no `Weil group`, no `local Langlands`, no `shtuka`, and the only `excursion` declarations in either tree are Tau Ceti's combinatorial excursion processes. What does exist is ambient machinery the roadmap would eventually sit on: Mathlib's condensed sets and modules with solidification (`Condensed`, `CondensedMod`, `CondensedMod.IsSolid`), derived and triangulated categories with Verdier localization, induced and coinduced representations with abelian Shapiro's lemma, dual root data (`RootPairing.flip`), the étale/pro-étale topologies with an ℓ-adic coefficient sheaf, and Haar measure; Tau Ceti's central simple algebras and Brauer group (including the division-algebra representative of a class), smooth discrete representations of a profinite group, Tate cohomology, and reductive group schemes with root data. The two most classically flavoured layers, ES7:function-field-automorphic and ES7:equal-characteristic, are the ones with the most usable inputs — division algebras, restricted products, Haar measure, function-field places — but neither their adelic constructions nor any of their theorems exist. Every layer is not built; ES0's centre target is partial.

targets.target: The algebra of natural endomorphisms of the identity of the enhanced category, its centrality and scalar structure
